title: Grey Heart Emoji 🩶 Meaning: Muted Love and Neutral Moods
description: 🩶 is the grey heart: understated affection, a neutral mood, or a match for silver and monochrome looks. See what it means in texts and how it differs from 🖤.
summary: The 🩶 grey heart emoji means quiet, understated affection. It suits people who find bright hearts too loud, and it can also suggest a flat, tired or uncertain mood. Much of its use is visual: silver, concrete, rainy skies, grey pets and monochrome outfits.
meaning: Grey is the least emphatic color a heart can be, and that is the point of 🩶. It lets someone say “I care” at low volume. People who dress in neutrals, keep minimalist feeds or simply dislike gushing use it as their everyday heart. From them it is not lukewarm; it is their normal register, in the same way a soft-spoken person is not being cold.

It can also describe a feeling. Grey days, grey moods and grey areas all lend it meaning. Someone posting 🩶 with a rain-streaked window or a lyric about numbness is reporting that things feel dull or heavy, a notch less dramatic than the black heart. In relationship talk it occasionally marks ambiguity, the situationship that is neither on nor off.

Before it was approved in 2022, the neutral hearts stopped at black and white. Grey filled the middle, which pleased designers and anyone posting photos of stone buildings, fog, wolves, elephants, silver jewelry or a grey tabby. Its official keywords include “silver” and “slate,” and it is a natural fit for silver anniversaries and proud captions about grey hair.

Some people use it gently in remembrance, as a softer alternative to black, though this is less established than 🖤 or 🤍 for condolences. It has no slang meaning and no fixed romantic code. Claims that a grey heart signals rejection or fading love describe one possible mood, not a rule. Most of the time the sender chose a color they liked.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: As a sign-off, 🩶 is calm and a little cool. Friends who avoid sentimentality use it for thanks and goodnights. If someone who normally sends colorful hearts switches to grey, they may be tired, low or keeping some distance, and a simple “you okay?” will tell you more than guessing.

contexts.label: In captions
contexts.body: Monochrome and “clean” aesthetics adopted it quickly. It sits under photos of city architecture, overcast beaches, grey sweatsuits, silver cars and brushed-metal gadgets, often in a row with 🖤 and 🤍. Pet accounts use it for grey cats, Weimaraners and rabbits. In all of these it is a color swatch in heart form.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: A grey heart is one of the hardest to read romantically because it says so little. It is friendly, and it may simply match their taste. It is not a typical flirting choice. If the person's words are warm, trust those. If everything about their messages feels as muted as the heart, interest may be limited.

contexts.label: For moods
contexts.body: On stories and in private accounts, 🩶 can stand for emotional flatness: burnout, a long winter, feeling stuck. It is honest without being alarming. People also use it for “grey area” situations, where they are unsure how they feel about a person or decision.

examples.text: Rainy Sunday, not leaving the couch 🩶
examples.meaning: A subdued, cozy mood matched to the weather.
A silver wedding anniversary, with grey standing in for silver.
Introducing a grey cat; the heart matches the fur.
Uncertainty about a relationship that sits in a grey area.
Pride in letting natural grey or silver hair show.

combos.meaning: A monochrome gradient for black-and-white photos or minimalist style.
Rainy-day mood, either cozy or a little down.
Affection for wolves, huskies or a team with a wolf mascot.
Silver sparkle: jewelry, anniversaries or shimmering grey outfits.

confusedWith.difference: 🖤 has attitude and tradition behind it: dark humor, goth style, mourning. 🩶 is softer and blanker, with less personality attached. On dark-mode screens the grey heart can look close to black, so the two are sometimes mistaken for each other.

🤍 reads as pure, clean and tender, and is established for sympathy and weddings. 🩶 is cooler and more neutral. On a white background the white heart often shows a grey outline, which adds to the mix-ups.
Someone feeling emotionally worn might consider either. ❤️‍🩹 specifically says healing is under way. 🩶 only says the color has drained out for now, with no promise of recovery.

avoid: Do not send it as your only response to exciting news; it can make you seem unenthusiastic.
Avoid it for a first romantic gesture, where its neutrality may be read as indifference.
Remember that older devices cannot display it and will show a blank box.
design: A solid heart in a medium, neutral grey, the same shape as the other plain hearts. Some vendors give it a faint silvery gradient; others keep it flat like slate. It was introduced in Emoji 15.0 alongside the pink and light blue hearts, completing a black, grey and white trio. Systems that predate that release show a placeholder instead.

faqs.q: What does 🩶 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: Most likely that she likes the color or keeps a neutral aesthetic. It is a quiet form of affection. If she usually sends brighter hearts and has switched to grey, she might be feeling flat or signaling a little distance, so check in.

faqs.q: What does 🩶 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Usually an understated “I appreciate you.” Men who find red or pink too sentimental sometimes settle on grey, black or blue. It does not carry a hidden meaning, and it is not a known code for rejection.
It can be. Grey suggests gloom, tiredness or numbness, and some people use it that way. Just as often it is about silver, rainy weather or a monochrome outfit. The caption or conversation decides.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🩶 and 🖤?
faqs.a: Black is bold: dark humor, alternative style, grief. Grey is subdued and noncommittal, a softer neutral. People who find the black heart too edgy but still want something without color often choose grey.

faqs.q: Is it spelled grey heart or gray heart?
faqs.a: Both work. The emoji's official name uses the British spelling “grey,” while American keyboards also find it under “gray.” Searching either word in an emoji picker should bring it up.
